title: Cueva de las Manos rock art, Argentina
summary: Cueva de las Manos is a rock-art site in Santa Cruz Province, Patagonia, overlooking the Río Pinturas canyon. Its painted hunting scenes and hand stencils belong to a stylistic sequence of more than 8,000 years that its researchers say begins 9,300 years before present. The site joined the World Heritage List in 1999.

uncertainty.note: Start is 9,300 years before present converted as 1950 minus 9,300; end is the last stylistic group, dated "some 1.300 years ago" (Onetto and Podestá), 1950 minus 1,300. Bradshaw Foundation instead says the art was executed between 13,000 and 9,500 years ago, so the start is disputed by sources.

when.display: sequence begins c. 9,300 years before present

where.modern_name: Cueva de las Manos, Río Pinturas canyon, Santa Cruz Province, Argentina
where.historical_name: Río Pinturas canyon, upper Deseado basin, Patagonia; no polity applies at the start of the sequence

importance.justification: One of the most important rock-art sequences of South America, listed as World Heritage in 1999 (Onetto and Podestá).
